stories.headline: Iran and Oman Discuss Strait of Hormuz Framework Amid Ongoing Conflict
stories.body:
Iranian and Omani foreign ministers discussed a framework agreement in Tehran. They spoke about setting up a temporary shipping corridor in the Strait of Hormuz. They also discussed clearing naval mines from the passage.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Tehran and Oman agreed on arrangements for the strait. They said the two sides agreed on sharing the waterway. They also agreed on sharing its revenues.

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi spoke about reopening the strait. He said the Strait of Hormuz will only reopen in exchange for clear actions. He said the war must end. He said the blockade must be lifted. He also said the situation in Yemen must be resolved.

Qatar's prime minister is scheduled to travel to Tehran soon. He aims to restart diplomatic negotiations between Iran and the United States.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian commented on the war. He said that the war must end at some point. He added that Iran still negotiates from a position of strength.

US President Donald Trump said that the war with Iran will continue. He said it will carry on for as long as necessary.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu expressed doubt about peace talks. He said he doubted negotiations could produce an agreement. He said this was due to Iran's current leadership.

Shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has dropped severely. Ship-tracking data showed that about 5 million barrels of oil per day passed through the strait on Monday. Before February 28, roughly 20 million barrels per day passed through the passage.

Data from ship tracker Kpler showed a similar slowdown. Kpler reported that only 112 oil and gas tankers passed through the strait between August 1 and August 19.

Safety in the waterway has also worsened. The UN's International Maritime Organization recorded 70 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. These incidents occurred since February 28. The organization reported that these events resulted in the deaths of 19 seafarers.

stories.headline: United States Imposes New Tariffs on Canadian Imports
stories.body:
The United States imposed new 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports. Trade negotiations collapsed before the US announced the decision.

US President Donald Trump said in an interview that it was time to teach Canada a lesson. He said Canada cannot continue its actions. Trump also announced 50 percent tariffs on Canadian autos and auto parts. Those tariffs will take effect on January 1.

US Vice President JD Vance spoke at a rally in Maine. He claimed that Canada and China are the two worst countries regarding trade policy. In a leaked audio recording, Vance called Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney a sweet guy who tries to out-tough Trump.

Carney said that Canada had been attacked. Canada announced retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on about $20 billion of US goods. These tariffs target US steel, dairy products, appliances, and farm equipment.

Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said Canada will match US tariffs dollar for dollar. The retaliatory tariffs will take effect on September 8. Annual trade between the two nations totals over $872 billion.

stories.headline: Hospital Fire in Islamabad Kills 14 Newborn Infants
stories.body:
A fire at a hospital maternity ward in Islamabad killed 14 newborn infants. The disaster occurred in the mother and child unit at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences.

Rescue officials said the fire started around 6:45 a.m.. An air-conditioning unit compressor exploded inside the nursery. Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said oxygen canisters inside the ward intensified the flames.

Hospital spokesperson Dr. Aneeza Jalil said 15 babies were in the ward when the fire broke out. She said a doctor saved one baby. Kamal confirmed that at least 14 babies died in the fire.

PIMS Executive Director Rana Imran Sikander spoke about safety at the facility. He said the ward door was manned rather than locked to prevent baby theft.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif suspended Federal Health Secretary Aslam Ghauri after the hospital fire.

stories.headline: Meta Reaches Multi-Billion Dollar Settlement With US States Over Teen Safety
stories.body:
Meta agreed to pay billions of dollars to settle lawsuits from US states over youth safety. France 24 reported that Meta agreed to pay $17 billion to settle claims from 47 states. Livemint reported a $16.68 billion settlement with 29 states. Al Jazeera put the total settlement figure at up to $17.1 billion.

The lawsuits accused Meta of causing social media addiction and harm to teenagers. They also made claims regarding child data collection.

Under the agreement, Meta will add daily time limits on Instagram and Facebook. It will also pause notifications during daytime school hours. Meta proposed a two-hour daily limit for users under 18 years old.

Meta said 30 percent of the payment depends on other companies. YouTube and TikTok must implement matching daily limits and safety features for Meta to pay that portion.

Meta previously faced legal penalties in New Mexico. A jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million in March. A judge ordered Meta to pay $567 million on August 6.

stories.headline: Syrian Democratic Forces Dissolve to Join State Military
stories.body:
The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces dissolved after merging with the Syrian state military. The group officially announced its dissolution on August 25, 2026.

SDF leader Mazloum Abdi made the announcement during a speech in Damascus. He spoke at the presidential palace.

The group was founded in 2015. It controlled large areas of northern Syria before the merger.

Under the agreement, SDF fighters will join the Syrian army under the Defence Ministry. The Asayish security forces will join the Interior Ministry.

SDF official Abdulkarim Omar spoke about the Women's Protection Units. He said the unit proposed joining the Interior Ministry as a specialized counterterrorism force.

The Turkish government commented on the dissolution. Turkey said the move is crucial for strengthening Syrian state authority and stability.

stories.headline: India and China Announce Eight-Point Consensus on Border Management
stories.body:
India and China announced an eight-point consensus on border management following high-level talks in Beijing. Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi co-chaired the special representatives meeting. Doval also met Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng before delegation talks.

Wang Yi used the phrase "Dragon-Elephant Dance" to describe cooperation despite differences.

The two nations agreed to establish two new military meeting points. They also agreed to open two new border military hotlines. In addition, they agreed to reopen three designated border trading points.

India thanked China for expanding batches for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra pilgrimage. Both sides agreed to hold the 26th round of talks in India in 2027.

The special talks mechanism began in 2003 to address the 3,488-kilometer border dispute. Tensions rose after a 2020 clash in Galwan Valley killed 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers. In October 2024, both sides agreed on border patrolling. That deal led to troop disengagement in eastern Ladakh.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in October 2024 and in 2025. India will host the BRICS Summit on September 12, 2026. China is building a $137-billion dam on the Brahmaputra river.
